# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 1

**1** This is the vision I saw, brothers and sisters: **2** After I had fasted for many days and prayed earnestly, asking God to show me the revelation he had promised me through the aged woman — that very night the aged woman appeared to me and said, "Because you hunger so greatly and are so eager to know, come early to the field where you farm in the morning, and at the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what it is necessary for you to see." **3** I asked her, "Lady, in which part of the field?" She said, "Wherever you wish." I chose a good and quiet place, but before I could speak further to give her the location, she said, "I will come wherever you wish." **4** So I went out to the field, brothers and sisters, counted the hours, and came to the place I had designated. There I saw a couch of ivory set there, on which lay a linen cushion with a covering of fine linen over it. **5** When I saw these things lying there with no one in the place, I was seized with wonder, and a trembling came over me and my hair stood on end. Since I was alone and had become frightened, I recovered myself and regained my composure. Then I saw the aged woman approaching with a small book in her hand; she sat down alone and greeted me: "Greetings, Hermas." **6** I answered in grief and weeping, "Greetings, my lady." She said, "Why so sad and gloomy, Hermas? You are patient and good-tempered and always cheerful." I said, "On account of an excellent woman who says I have sinned against her." **7** She replied, "Far be that from a servant of God! But the thought did arise in your heart. Such a thought is precisely what brings sin upon the servants of God. For it is an evil and shameful purpose when a righteous person harbors a wicked desire — and all the more so for Hermas, who is temperate and abstains from every wicked desire and is known for simplicity and great innocence." **8** "But God is not displeased with you only for this reason — it is also so that your household may repent, for they have sinned against the Lord and against you their parents. Yet you love your children and failed to admonish your household; and for this reason the Lord is displeased with you. But he will restore all the former failures of your household, for through their sins and iniquities you have been worn down by the cares of this life. But the great mercy of the Lord has taken pity on you, and will establish you and your household, and strengthen you before his glory."

---

### Council Notes

Vision 2 begins with careful scene-setting: the ivory couch, the linen, the appointed time. These suggest Hermas preparing for a formal encounter — perhaps echoing the preparation for liturgical or prophetic reception.

The "fifth hour" appointment (roughly 11 AM) is a precise detail of dailiness embedded in an apocalyptic narrative — a characteristic Hermaic quality.

The repetition of the household-sin material from Vision 1 is not error but reinforcement. The double communication confirms the seriousness of both charges: Hermas's internal desire and his parental negligence.
